title: Starter credit & micro-tier pricing notes
content:
Purpose: rough, single-person scratchpad for a low-friction starter package + onboarding credits aimed at small businesses and early PLG signups. Not a proposal; just numbers + ideas to test with product/growth.

Context / goals:
- convert self-serve signups to paid within 14–30 days
- keep first-dollar friction low (easy to experiment w/ product)
- avoid heavy discounting of committed capacity while still giving tangible value
- keep unit economics breakeven target: >50% gross margin after infra and caching improvements

High-level ideas to explore:
1) Tiny free credit for new accounts (e.g., $7 equivalent) that maps to token credit rather than time-limited credits.
2) Starter monthly plan for "small apps" (1–3 developers) — low commitment, built-in burst credits, modest included tokens.
3) Pay-as-you-go (default) with optional auto-convert to starter plan after hitting a usage threshold.
4) Usage package bundles: tokens + request concurrency / faster tier as add-ons.

Assumptions (very rough, to iterate):
- infra (hosted) cost to serve: $0.0025 per 1k tokens (after batching, KV cache savings for typical chat/workload).
- marginal storage & infra ops amortized: ~$0.0003 per 1k tokens.
- total unit cost baseline: $0.0028 per 1k tokens.
- retail target price (bench): $0.02 per 1k tokens for lowest non-committed plan (~85% gross margin target initially).
- average session = 750 tokens (150 prompt + 600 response) for a small app chat flow.

Token math examples:
- Cost to serve one typical session: 0.75 * ($0.0028 per 1k) = 0.75 * 0.0028 = $0.0021 per session.
- Retail price if charged at $0.02 per 1k tokens: 0.75 * 0.02 = $0.015 per session.
- Gross margin per session: (0.015 - 0.0021) / 0.015 = ~86% (good headroom to subsidize starter credits).

Starter plan (sketch): "Starter" – $29 / month
- Included: 1,500,000 tokens (~2k sessions at 750 tokens)
- Equivalent token price: $29 / 1.5M = $0.0193 per 1k tokens (~aligns w/ $0.02 retail).
- Overage: $0.025 per 1k tokens.
- Burst credits: +100k tokens as monthly "burst" pool for spiky usage
- Limits: 2 concurrent streams, 90-day rollback for trial conversions

Economics for Starter plan (back-of-envelope):
- Monthly infra cost for included tokens: 1,500 * 0.0028 = $4.20 (since 1,500k tokens * $0.0028 per 1k) -> wait math: compute precisely: (1,500,000 / 1,000) * 0.0028 = 1500 * 0.0028 = $4.20.
- Gross margin on included tokens: $29 - $4.20 = $24.80 -> ~85.5% margin on included usage (high).
- If average Starter customer uses 500k tokens -> revenue recognized portion: (500/1500) * $29 = $9.67 realized; infra cost = (500 * 0.0028) = (500k/1k*0.0028)=500*0.0028 = $1.40 -> margin on realized usage still strong.

Free credit offer idea:
- New signups get $7 of token credit (non-stackable) mapped to ~350k tokens at $0.02 per 1k.
- Cost to us: infra for 350k tokens = (350 * 0.0028) = $0.98.
- If 3% of free-credit users convert to Starter within 30d, CAC subsidy can be small and pay back quickly.

Alternative micro-tier: pay-monthly micro plan ($9/mo)
- Included 300k tokens, overage $0.03 per 1k, 1 concurrent stream.
- Infra cost for included tokens: 300 * 0.0028 = $0.84 -> margin ok if average churn < 60% month1

Trigger-based auto-upgrade flow (product idea):
- If a PAYG user spends >$12 in 14 days, prompt: "Switch to Starter for $29/mo and save X%" showing break-even token counts.
- Provide one-click conversion and transfer remaining credits pro-rated.

Key levers & experiments to run:
- Experiment A: $7 credit vs $12 credit. Track conversion -> Starter and conversion -> paid overall. Measure net CAC.
- Experiment B: Starter price $29 vs $39 with different included tokens (1.5M vs 2.5M). Measure ARPU and churn.
- Experiment C: Overage price elasticities (0.02 vs 0.03) — measure revenue when users exceed included tokens.
- Experiment D: Make caching-enabled models default for Starter to reduce unit cost on typical patterns.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate infra cost assumptions with infra team and real traces (batch factor, cache hit rates).
- How do embeddings usage and long-context models change the averages? Need separate tiering for embedding-heavy apps.
- Policy for unused included tokens on cancellation/upgrade? (prorate?)
- Billing cadence for burst credits: monthly reset vs rolling window?
- How to present effective per-1k pricing clearly in the UI (avoid confusion around tokens vs messages).

Notes to self:
- Keep starter price psychologically anchored at $29 (common SaaS anchor).
- Keep free-credit small but meaningful — aim to let devs build a quick sample app or call the chat flow ~20–30x.
- Track 14-day retention and 30-day paid conversion as primary success metrics for these offers.

Quick sensitivity table (manual mental calc):
- If infra cost double (0.0056 per 1k) -> Starter margin on included tokens drops to ~70% but still acceptable initially.
- If average session grows to 1250 tokens (bigger responses) -> sessions per 1.5M tokens drop from 2k -> 1200 sessions. Evaluate UX tradeoffs and sample prompts in onboarding to keep sizes small.

Action items:
- Ask infra for a cost dump: real per-1k at 1k/10k/100k/1M token volume with caching on/off (due 2026-03-10).
- Wire up simple product modal copy and A/B test flow.
- Add micro-plan to pricing page as experiment (feature flag).

End of scratchpad.

(FYI: this is a single-user scratchpad; share selectively.)
